posts.text:
Good morning.
One thing at a time today.

posts.quote: All that we are is the result of what we have thought.
posts.author: The Dhammapada
posts.caption:
This line is over 2,000 years old and it's the reason this page is called Thought's.

The full verse goes on: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts.

We named the page after that idea back in 2021. Same idea, new home. Daily quotes, short poems and life lines from people who said it first and said it best.

Follow along this week. Four posts a day, all of them short.

#buddha #motivationalquotes #dailyquotes

posts.quote:
If you can keep your head when all about you
are losing theirs and blaming it on you...
posts.author: Rudyard Kipling, If, 1910

posts.text:
You don't need a new life.
You need ten quiet minutes
with the one you have.
posts.caption:
Before you change everything, try ten quiet minutes.

No phone, no plan, no podcast in your ears. Tea, a window, whatever's around.

Most of us are not unhappy with our life. We're just never in it long enough to notice.

Try it today and tell me how it went.

#lifequotes #inspiration #selfgrowth

deck.sub: Written up to 2,500 years ago. Still true on a Monday.
deck.stake: Five people who never had a phone said the most useful things about having one.
slides: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.
Epictetus, Enchiridion
The news isn't the stress. The story we add to it is.
Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years.
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations
Written by an emperor, to himself, while away at war.
Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
Ralph Waldo Emerson, Self-Reliance
Not a holiday, not a person, not a purchase.
A man's ability to remain in one place and linger in his own company.
Seneca, Letters
His sign of a well-ordered mind. Try ten minutes.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Lao Tzu, Tao Te Ching
One step. Not a plan for all thousand miles.

posts.author: Seneca
posts.caption:
Seneca wrote this to a friend who was scared of things that hadn't happened yet.

The full line: there are more things likely to frighten us than there are to crush us.

Think of the last thing you dreaded for a week. How long did the actual thing take? Ten minutes? An hour?

Showing up on a bad day is a win. Count it.

Not every day is a good day. Some days you just get out of bed, do the minimum and go back.

That still counts. The streak is what matters, not the score.

deck.cover: Emily Dickinson wrote hope as a bird
deck.stake: She wrote around 1,800 poems and published fewer than a dozen while she was alive.
slides: "Hope" is the thing with feathers -
Not a feeling. A small, light thing that lands on you.
That perches in the soul -
It doesn't move in. It perches. Ready to fly, but staying.
And sings the tune without the words -
Hope rarely explains itself. It just hums.
And never stops - at all -
Even on the bad days. Listen for it.
deck.recap_poem:
"Hope" is the thing with feathers -
That perches in the soul -
And sings the tune without the words -
And never stops - at all -
deck.cta: Share it with someone who needs a little bird today.

posts.caption:
Emily Dickinson wrote hope as a bird. Read it one line at a time.

One of the best known poems about hope in English, and it's only the first stanza.

She didn't title it. She almost never titled anything. The world just started calling it by its first line.

Share it with someone who needs a little bird today.

#emilydickinson #poetry #quotesabouthope #classicpoetry

Quotes about hope usually come from people who had it easy. This one didn't.

deck.cover: The most misread poem in English
deck.sub: Robert Frost, The Road Not Taken, 1916
deck.stake: Everyone quotes the last line as a pep talk. Frost was being sly.
slides:
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I -
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.
The famous part. Sounds like: be brave, be different.

Though as for that the passing there
Had worn them really about the same,
Earlier in the poem. Both roads were the same.

I shall be telling this with a sigh
Somewhere ages and ages hence:
The sigh is the point. He'll tell the story later, and make it sound bigger.
Choose a road. Then be kind about the story you tell.
Frost wrote it as a gentle joke for his friend Edward Thomas, who could never pick a path.
recap: Both roads were about the same
We decide what it meant later
deck.cta: Did you know this? Yes or no in the comments.

posts.caption:
The Road Not Taken doesn't say what most people think it says.

Robert Frost's most famous poem is quoted at graduations as advice to be different. Read the middle stanza and the roads were 'really about the same'.

It's about how we tell our life story afterwards. Which might be a better lesson.

Did you know this? Tell me yes or no below.

#robertfrost #poetry #theroadnottaken #classicpoetry

deck.cover: 6 lines from old books worth keeping
deck.sub: Read one a day. Or all six now.
deck.stake: Each of these has outlived the person who wrote it by a century or more.
slides: If one advances confidently in the direction of his dreams, he will meet with a success unexpected in common hours.
Henry David Thoreau, Walden
The real line behind every 'follow your dreams' poster.
Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
Ralph Waldo Emerson, Self-Reliance
You already know more than you're giving yourself credit for.
The unexamined life is not worth living.
Socrates, in Plato's Apology
Said at his own trial. He didn't take it back.
We know what we are, but know not what we may be.
William Shakespeare, Hamlet
You're not finished. Nobody is.
How wonderful it is that nobody need wait a single moment before starting to improve the world.
Anne Frank
Written at 14, in hiding.
Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.
Swami Vivekananda
From the Katha Upanishad, made famous by him.
deck.cta: Save it. Read one each morning this week.

posts.caption:
Six lines from old books that are worth more than most new ones.

Thoreau, Emerson, Socrates, Shakespeare, Anne Frank and Swami Vivekananda. Famous quotes with the sources, so you can go read the rest.

deck.cover: A small guide to bad days
deck.stake: You don't need to solve the day. You need to land it.
slides: Drink water before you decide anything.
Half of bad moods are just thirst and no lunch.
Lower the bar to one task.
One. Do it. The day now has a win in it.
Text one person. Not everyone.
Pick the one who doesn't need an explanation.
Go outside for ten minutes.
Phone in your pocket. Look at something far away.
Don't read old messages tonight.
Bad days rewrite the past. Leave it alone.
Sleep early. It's the reset button.
Tomorrow-you will thank you.
